body:
Note that this would be inconsistent with python `or` behavior, which is a null coalescing operator there (see also https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/1321). Using `or` for null coalescing has been rejected in https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/1887, and we do not guarantee consistency with python syntax, but it still might be worth considering.

But yea, considering `if a:` auto-truthifies the argument `a`, I can see why users might expect `a or b` to auto-truthify its arguments `a` and `b`.

Edit: Huh, considering `a and b` booleanize in the https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/108813 example, I guess we do already make this decision.
